title: test-0003-GEN-SLEEP
passage: Many people mistakenly believe that sleep is merely a period where the body and brain switch off like a machine, but this is far from the truth. During sleep, your brain remains highly active, processing the information you learned during the day and strengthening your memory. This is why a good night's sleep is essential for academic success, rather than staying awake all night to study. Furthermore, your body clock is not just controlled by how tired you feel; it is deeply influenced by light. Exposure to the blue light emitted by screens, such as phones and tablets, tricks your brain into thinking it is still daytime, making it difficult to fall asleep. Additionally, sleep needs change as you grow. While adults might function on different schedules, teenagers experience a natural shift in their body clock, causing them to feel alert later at night. It is also a myth that you can simply 'catch up' on lost sleep by sleeping in on the weekend. Sleep debt accumulates, and your body requires consistent, daily rest to repair tissues and support healthy growth. Relying on caffeine or sugar before bed further disrupts your natural cycle, preventing the deep, restorative sleep your body needs to function at its best the next day.
summary: Many people mistakenly believe that sleep is merely a period where the body and brain switch off like a machine, but this is far from the truth. Relying on caffeine or sugar before bed can make you sleep less, so you need to sleep more the next day.
